deep.reconstruction:
Context: Gauss's Hanover survey. The previous page adjusts station directions; the next page tabulates log r, log α and log b against latitude around P = 51°31'48.7". Krüger's pencil note 'Band IX S.137' points to the printed version in Gauss, Werke IX. The page sets up the ellipsoidal conformal conic projection (the 'second mode of representing the spheroid, referred to a parallel circle') and the chord–arc reduction of directions.

(1) Ellipsoid constants (Walbeck ellipsoid, flattening f = 1/302.78, axis ratio b/a = 301.78/302.78).
- The meridian quadrant is Q = (π/2) a / (1 + e²/4 + 7e⁴/64 + 15e⁶/256 + 579e⁸/16384 + 1515e¹⁰/65536 + …). This is the reciprocal of the usual series 1 − e²/4 − 3e⁴/64 − 5e⁶/256 − 175e⁸/16384 − 441e¹⁰/65536, i.e. Q = a·E(e²).
- log e² = 7.8191850400−10, where e² = 1 − (301.78/302.78)². Krüger corrects the last digits to …399.
- log √(1−e²) = 9.9985632696−10.
- Q = 10⁷ m by the definition of the metre. Hence (π/2)a = 10⁷·(1 + 0.0016486370240 + 0.0000047565066 + 0.0000000168038 + …) = 10016534.104015 m, called the 'Erd-Äquatorsquadrant'.
- log of this = 7.0007174740. Subtracting log(π/2) = 0.1961198770 gives log a = 6.8045975970 (metres), a ≈ 6376851 m.
- Adding log(toise/metre)⁻¹ = 9.7101917226−10 gives log a = 6.5147893196 (toises).

(2) Notation. P = latitude of the principal (standard) parallel; m = scale ratio; λ, φ = longitude and latitude of a point; x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ are the plane coordinates; R = r(P); μ = sin P (cone constant); sin u = e sin φ, sin U = e sin P.

(3) Projection.
- θ = μλ.
- Conformality requires m = μ r √(1−e² sin²φ)/(a cos φ), so r/m = a cos φ/(μ cos u).
- Requiring m(P) = 1 gives R = a cos P/(μ √(1−e² sin²P)) = a cos P/(μ cos U) = a/(cos U tan P), using μ = sin P.
- The integrated radius is r = k tan(45°−φ/2)^μ ((1+e sin φ)/(1−e sin φ))^{μe/2} = k tan(45°−φ/2)^μ tan(45°+u/2)^{μe}, since √((1+sin u)/(1−sin u)) = tan(45°+u/2).
- r(P) = R fixes k = a tan(45°+P/2)^μ / (cos U · tan(45°+U/2)^{μe} · tan P).
- Differentiating: dr/r = −μ(1−e²) dφ / ((1−e² sin²φ) cos φ).
- dm/m = (sin φ − μ)/cos φ · (1−e²)/(1−e² sin²φ) dφ = (dr/r)(1 − sin φ/μ). Gauss first started a wrong numerator and struck it.

(4) Direction reduction.
- Let ζ be the grid azimuth of a geodesic element, reckoned against the image of the first meridian. Along an ellipsoidal geodesic the azimuth obeys dα = sin φ dλ (step mine). The local meridian image is rotated by θ = μλ.
- Hence dζ = dθ − sin φ dλ = (1 − sin φ/μ) dθ, which Gauss writes as 6q dθ.
- Assume 6q varies linearly along the line (step mine). The chord direction is then ζ° + Δθ∫₀¹(1−t)·6q(t) dt = ζ° + (2q°+q')Δθ.
- So Z = ζ° + (2q°+q')(θ'−θ°), and from the other end Z = 180° + ζ' + (q°+2q')(θ°−θ'). This is the classical (2q+q') arc-to-chord formula.

(5) Series for 6q = 1 − sin φ/μ. Put ρ = ln(r/R) and r = R(1+δ), and let A = (1−e²μ²)(1−μ²)/((1−e²)μ²).
- 6q = Aρ + (1+e²−2e²μ²)(1−e²μ²)(1−μ²)/((1−e²)²μ²) ρ² − [1+e² − 3(1+4e²+e⁴)μ² + 15e²(1+e²)μ⁴ − 14e⁴μ⁶](1−e²μ²)(1−μ²)/(3(1−e²)³μ⁴) ρ³ …
- 6q = Aδ + (1+3e²−4e²μ²)(1−e²μ²)(1−μ²)/(2(1−e²)²μ²) δ² − [1+e² − (1+10e²+7e⁴)μ² + (9e²+21e⁴)μ⁴ − 14e⁴μ⁶](1−e²μ²)(1−μ²)/(3(1−e²)³μ⁴) δ³ …
- Both are Taylor expansions about φ = P, using ds/dρ = −(1−s²)(1−e²s²)/(μ(1−e²)) with s = sin φ (derivation mine). The δ-series follows from ρ = δ − δ²/2 + δ³/3.
- The brackets above are as Krüger corrected them; Gauss's originals are given in the errors list.

(6) Practical form. Most conveniently put q = α(r−R)√r and tabulate log α. Its constant part is 8.9648149933, and the next page shows log α ≈ 8.9648150 at P. Alternatively one may equally well use q = α r log(r/R).
errors: ρ³ coefficient: Gauss wrote 15(1+ee)(1+ee)μ⁴. The correct term is 15ee(1+ee)μ⁴, coming from g'(μ) with g(s) = s(1+e²−2e²s²)(1−s²)(1−e²s²). Krüger's marginal correction 'muss heissen: 15ee(1+ee)' is right.
δ³ coefficient: Gauss wrote (1+6ee+7e⁴)μμ. Re-expanding the ρ-series gives (1+10ee+7e⁴)μμ. Krüger's '+10ee' note is right; the other δ³ terms (9ee+21e⁴, −14e⁴μ⁶) check out.
log e² 7.8191850400: Krüger annotates the last digits as …399. This is a rounding-level difference in the 10th decimal.
The (2q°+q') formula assumes 6q is linear in a parameter along which θ also grows uniformly. It is an approximation of second order in the line length, not exact; this is standard and acceptable.

I could not reproduce the stated constant log α = 8.9648149933 from the leading coefficient A/(6R^{3/2}) in any obvious units. The unit conventions for q (seconds or radians) and for r are not fully clear from the page, so this number is left unverified rather than called an error.

results.what: Meridian quadrant Q = (π/2)a/(1+e²/4+7e⁴/64+15e⁶/256+579e⁸/16384+1515e¹⁰/65536…), used to get a from Q = 10⁷ m on the Walbeck ellipsoid (f = 1/302.78)
results.modern_name: meridian arc (complete elliptic integral of the second kind) series

results.what: Conformal conic projection of the ellipsoid: θ = μλ, μ = sin P, r = k tan(45°−φ/2)^μ tan(45°+u/2)^{μe}, true scale on parallel P, plus scale differential dm/m
results.modern_name: ellipsoidal Lambert conformal conic projection (one standard parallel)
results.usually_credited_to: Lambert 1772 (sphere); ellipsoidal form Gauss (published in Werke IX, 1903, ed. Krüger)

results.what: Grid-azimuth change of geodesic dζ = (1−sin φ/μ)dθ and chord-direction reduction Z = ζ° + (2q°+q')Δθ
results.modern_name: arc-to-chord (t−T) correction for a conformal conic projection

results.what: Power series of 6q = 1−sin φ/μ in ρ = ln(r/R) and in δ = r/R−1 to third order
results.modern_name: series expansion of meridian convergence / curvature term in the projection radius

deep.surprise_reason: This is Gauss's well-known ellipsoidal conformal conic for the Hanover survey. Krüger's own annotation cites its publication in Werke IX p.137, so the material is known and published. The only extra detail is that Gauss's two third-order coefficients contain slips, which Krüger corrected.

checkable.asserts: meridian quadrant Q = a*E(e^2) = (pi/2) a (1 - e^2/4 - ...)

transcription_corrections: 'Für q hat man die Reihen' is most likely 'Für 6q hat man die Reihen' (image reads 'Fürbq'); the series' leading term matches 1−sinφ/μ = 6q.
In dm/m the struck numerator is a cancelled first attempt; the intended numerator is (sin φ − μ).
'∂ζ = (1 − sinφ/μ)∂θ = 6q∂θ' is confirmed; ζ is the grid azimuth against the first meridian.
Krüger's pencil '399 Kr' next to log ee 7.8191850 400 is a correction of the last digits; 'Kr' marks and 'Band IX S.137' are editorial (Krüger) annotations, not Gauss.
Margin note 'muss heissen: 15ee(1+ee) Kr' applies to the term 15(1+ee)(1+ee)μ⁴; '+10ee Kr' applies to (1+6ee+7e⁴)μμ in the δ³ term.
Final lines: '[A]m bequemsten setzt man…', '[D]er constante Theil…', '[Es]ist eben so bequem q = α r log(r/R)'.
